title: Virtual Townhall: Combating Attacks on the Federal Work Force
description:
Join Democratic Attorneys General, AFGE President Everett Kelley, and candidate for Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones for a virtual town hall moderated by D.C. Attorney General Brian Schwalb on the importance of Democratic AGs as they fight to protect the federal workforce against DOGE firings and Donald Trump’s illegal mass layoffs.  

After the Trump administration and Elon Musk began firing probationary employees, gutting the Department of Education, and slashing positions and programs they didn’t like, Democratic AGs sued — and won many universal injunctions. But as courts move away from issuing these nation-spanning injunctions, Virginia federal employees are being left high and dry under Republican AG Jason Miyares, who refuses to stand up to Trump. Hundreds of thousands of federal employees and federal jobs are housed in Virginia, and as Trump hacks and slashes, Virginia is suffering. That’s why Democratic AGs are coming together with AFGE to deliver one simple message: Elect Jay Jones in November if you want an AG that protects workers instead of doing Trump’s bidding.  

Since Inauguration Day, Democratic AGs have sued to protect everyday Americans over 40 times. They continue to rack up win after win because they are on the right side of the law and the US Constitution -- the People’s side. The fight needs more fighters, and Virginia needs Jay Jones to join the ranks of Democratic AGs in November.

The numbers at play here are almost unimaginable but the hurt will be real. Food assistance will dwindle and health insurance plans will see widespread restrictions.

There are real consequences for our natural and built environments, too. That's why the Michigan Environmental Council, Michigan League of Conservation Voters and Sierra Club Michigan Chapter are coming together to talk about them in "Flood Proof."

In this webinar series, we wade through the deluge of federal news and dredge up what it means for Michigan. We will also share ways organizations and individuals are protecting air, water and beloved places from it all.

So join us in our next webinar, where we will discuss the "Big, Beautiful Bill" and other recent cuts and rollbacks. The Environmental Council does not often get involved in federal decisionmaking, but this is a watershed moment in Michigan history and it must be addressed.
